_meta.description: CVD-safe swatch palette shared by pixi run console (api/task_console.jl) and pixi run recital-console (python/cecelia/effectiveness/console.py). Do not add or remove keys without updating both consoles — each maps swatches to its own semantic slots (statuses, mechanisms, outcomes). The 8-colour ANSI palette is remapped by the user's terminal theme, so both consoles emit 24-bit truecolor escapes seeded from these hexes.
peer_palettes: app/src/gating/popmanager/clustering_colour.jl :: OKABE_ITO — positional Vector{String}[8], categorical population-colour assignment; 8th slot is '#000000' black (this file's 8th slot is grey for terminal chrome).
frontend/src/plots/palettes.json :: okabe-ito — positional array[8], same hues, same black-at-8 as the Julia one; consumed by the frontend plot renderer.
frontend/src/utils/landscape.ts :: LANDSCAPE_SWATCHES — 5-key semantic subset (dark/bright-uniform/bright-textured/edge/mixed) for the landscape overlay legend.

frontend/src/style.css :: --cc-dot-ok/-warn/-fail/-idle/-info (.cc-dot tones) — the app's status lights: sky_blue/orange/vermillion/grey/blue (good is sky blue, as in both consoles); pinned to this file by frontend/src/utils/statusDot.test.ts.
_meta.why_a_fourth_home: Each peer is positional or shape-different (semantic-named vs categorical-indexed) or lives in a runtime this file can't reach cheaply — api/task_console.jl deliberately doesn't `using Cecelia` for boot cost, so the Julia OKABE_ITO const isn't a one-line swap. If you re-tune a hue here, update every listed peer in the same change and vice versa; the CVD guarantee assumes they don't drift.

_badges: Identity, not meaning: one per live Claude Code session in the recital console's agents pane (`agents.session_badge`). Paul Tol's 'bright' scheme (https://personal.sron.nl/~pault/), CVD-safe like the swatches. The hues overlap the swatches' (cyan ~ sky_blue, rose ~ vermillion, sand ~ yellow); the badge's own column is what tells it from a state. Python only.
